This is a great co-op game with some of the best, most detailed pixel art I think I've seen in a modern side-scroller. The parallax background especially is to be noted, but they've nailed the whole '90s era retro game aesthetic here.

The gameplay is excellent, with boss mechanics that are both varied, fun and at times challenging. The auto-save triggers are spaced out in all the right places though, so it never gets frustrating dying.

I played the game on an older TV, which unintentionally made the game look even better. The soundtrack by Tommy Gustafsson is also bangin'. Very recommended.

Unpolished, full of bug, badly optimized compared to the first game. the new roaming boss system feels really lackluster and full of bug. The final act is a mess, the narrator speaks to slow compared to the cutscene. If u don't wanna play a mediocre unoptimised game i don't reccommend this one, the first game is way better

I bought this thinking it would be a chill little golf game to relax with my friends. So obviously I turned collision on and messed with the gravity. That was the moment it stopped being Golf with Friends and became Golf with Enemies. Nothing brings people closer than hearing your friends scream on Discord because you accidentally on purpose knocked their ball across the map.

We were crying laughing the whole time, roasting each other, hitting impossible shots, and at one point I literally launched my ball straight into a pharaoh’s mouth. It’s such a simple game, but playing it with my friends, just chilling and losing our minds together, made it one of the funniest nights we’ve had. 10 out of 10 would absolutely risk the friendships again.

If the screenshots grab your attention at all, give the game a shot. For the price of a coffee, it's worth it to support small games.

I was craving a new metroidvania to play and so far Gigasword has scratched that itch. The intro is pretty long, between cutscenes, dialogue, and just the time it takes to really get to interesting enemies and puzzles. Some of the cutscene illustrations of the main hero are funny looking, but that's a minor note. Now that I'm in the castle more I enjoy it a lot. There are smart puzzles utilizing the sword. The combat feels nice with weight behind the sword.

RIP Viktor Antonov... Your work made us discover the beauty of Dunwall which still remains one of my favorite places in a video game.

For players: 
Delete logs from the path below manually. 
 %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\MetalEden\Saved\Logs 
or
 GAME_ROOT_PATH\MetalEden\Saved\Logs 

- You can also find save file from the directory above them. Make backup accordingly. 
- Logs are about 6~10 Gib for one playthrough. 
- Lack of disk space (due to the heavy logging) will fail to keep your save.

Furi isn't an easy type of game (unless you're playing on promenade difficulty), but it is one that is fair, fun, and most of all: challenging.

If you're the type of gamer that enjoys playing a tough game, where mastering and playing it rewards you, then Furi is absolutely perfect.

I'd pay it homage to videogames that would kick your teeth in until you got better at it, or quit.

This is for those that don't give up.

It really is a good John Wick simulator, rough around the edges but lots of good options to keep it fun and playable at any difficulty level. This is what we need more of instead of massive, expensive-to-develop AAA titles that are overly obsessed with graphics.
